title: An AI agent that runs simulation experiments — and can't fool you
description: A tool-calling agent proposes screening runs and A/B experiments on the help-desk simulation and writes a summary. A job pipeline decides everything else: contract gate, budget gate, seeded runs in an append-only registry, replications from a target CI half-width, and a claim check of every sentence.
outcome: You can put an LLM agent in front of a stochastic simulator without letting it decide anything: arguments validated against a contract and an envelope, cost reserved before running, n chosen from statistics, every published number traced to a reproducible run, and overstated claims rejected.
environment: Python 3.12 (validated on 3.12.15, Linux x86_64) + numpy 2.5.3; reuses simulation L100 #6 / L200 #10 / L300 #14, ai-agents L200 #8 / L300 #14 and kb/shared/local_agent (fake model server) via _kb.py; optional Ollama (OpenAI-compatible /v1, tools supported) for --real-model
overview: The agent may ask for any experiment and write any sentence; code decides what runs, how many times, at what cost, and which sentences anyone reads. The failure lab is the classic one: 'significant improvement' from 3 replications.
prerequisites: ai-agents L100 #6 A minimal agent loop and L200 #8 (tool schemas)
simulation L200 #10 (replications and confidence intervals) and L300 #14 (Morris)

designBrief.context: A help desk (M/M/1, lam 0.8/min, mu 1.0/min, 30 tickets waiting on Monday) is considering a triage script that makes service 5% faster (mu 1.05). An agent plans the experiments and writes the report for the manager; a local model may hallucinate numbers and overstate results.
constraints: 100% of numeric claims in the published report trace to a registered run
every registered run reproduces bit-for-bit from its record (same environment fingerprint)
session budget 300,000 simulated customers and 8 model calls - never exceeded, reserved before running
'significant' only with >= 10 replications per arm and a 95% Welch CI of the difference that excludes 0; target half-width <= 0.3 min
proposals outside the schema or the verified envelope (lam/mu <= 0.9) never run and cost nothing
the model sees only the brief and tool results - no keys, no data files
designBrief.question: How do you let an agent drive simulation experiments while guaranteeing that every number and every 'significant' in its report is true?

architecture.summary: agent.py (ai-agents L100 #6 loop, L300 #14 Budget) sends tool calls to a job pipeline. contract.py validates them with the ai-agents L200 #8 validator against the same schemas the model receives, plus the envelope rule lam/mu <= 0.9 (verified in M1). SimBudget reserves cost in simulated customers before any run. pipeline.py runs the simulation L200 #10 help desk with seeds keyed by SeedSequence(root, spawn_key=(arm, rep)) and the L300 #14 Morris code through an adapter, sizes replications with solution/replications.py, and writes runs and experiment facts to an append-only JSONL registry (run_id = sha256 of model, version, params, seed; value as float.hex). claims.py checks every summary sentence against the cited experiment's facts and verdict; rejected sentences are replaced by code-written lines. run_project.py prints a JSON-lines scorecard: 5 milestones, 4 seams, 3 fitness functions.

code:
"""L600 #03: an AI agent that runs simulation experiments - and can't fool you.

The agent (a tool-calling loop) proposes screening runs and A/B experiments on the L200 #10 help-desk simulation and
writes a summary. Code decides everything else: the contract gate (schema + verified envelope), the budget gate,
seeded runs into an append-only registry, replications sized from a target CI half-width, and a claim check of
every sentence. Prints one JSON line per milestone, seam and fitness function; exits 1 on any failure.
python run_project.py [--inject few-reps|unseeded|no-contract|no-budget-gate] [--real-model]
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import agent
import claims
import model
import pipeline
import registry as reg
import stats

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT = HERE / "out"
BRIEF = ("Help-desk study, seed 13. Screen with sobol 64. Screen with morris 10. "
         "Compare mu 1.0 vs 1.05 at lam 0.8 with 3 replications. Compare mu 1.0 vs 1.05 at lam 0.97 with 3 replications.")
SIM_BUDGET, HALF_WIDTH, MAX_CALLS = 300_000, 0.3, 8  # customers per session; min; agent model calls
FAULTS = ("few-reps", "unseeded", "no-contract", "no-budget-gate")


def verify_model():
    """M1 (L100 #6 V&V): 95% CI of 10 long runs must cover the M/M/1 formula; same seed -> same bits."""
    rows = []
    for rho in (0.5, 0.8, 0.9):
        p = {"lam": rho, "mu": 1.0, "backlog": 0, "customers": 20_000, "warmup": 2_000}
        m, h = stats.mean_ci([model.run_once(p, model.seed_for(6, 0, r)) for r in range(10)])
        rows.append({"rho": rho, "sim": round(m, 3), "half_width": round(h, 3), "formula": round(model.mm1_wq(rho, 1.0), 3),
                     "covered": abs(m - model.mm1_wq(rho, 1.0)) <= h})
    p = {"lam": 0.8, "mu": 1.0}
    same = model.run_once(p, 123).hex() == model.run_once(p, 123).hex()
    return rows, same


def session(inject, real_model, registry):
    pl = pipeline.Pipeline(registry, pipeline.SimBudget(SIM_BUDGET, gate=inject != "no-budget-gate"),
                           half_width=HALF_WIDTH, policy=pipeline.naive_policy if inject == "few-reps" else None,
                           gate=inject != "no-contract", seeded=inject != "unseeded")
    server = None
    if real_model:
        url, name = os.environ.get("LOCAL_MODEL_URL", "http://localhost:11434/v1"), os.environ.get("LOCAL_MODEL", "qwen2.5:1.5b")
    else:
        import fake_sim_agent
        (server, url), name = fake_sim_agent.start_in_thread(), "fake-model"
    try:
        out = agent.run_session(BRIEF, pl, url, name, max_calls=MAX_CALLS)
    finally:
        if server:
            server.shutdown()
            server.server_close()
    return pl, out


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--inject", choices=FAULTS)
    ap.add_argument("--real-model", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=OUT)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    out_dir = args.out
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (out_dir / "registry.jsonl").unlink(missing_ok=True)  # fresh registry per run (append-only within a run)
    registry = reg.Registry(out_dir / "registry.jsonl")
    lines = []

    def score(kind, name, passed, **measures):
        lines.append({kind: name, "pass": bool(passed), **measures})
        print(json.dumps(lines[-1]))

    v_rows, same = verify_model()
    pl, out = session(args.inject, args.real_model, registry)
    rows, published = claims.review(out["summary"], registry)
    rejected_jobs = [j for j in pl.jobs if j["states"][-1] == "REJECTED"]
    by_contract = [j["job"] for j in rejected_jobs if "VALIDATED" not in j["states"]]
    by_budget = [j["job"] for j in rejected_jobs if "VALIDATED" in j["states"]]
    runs_rejected = sum(r["job"] in by_contract + by_budget for r in registry.runs())
    outside = [j["job"] for j in pl.jobs if j["tool"] == "run_experiment" and "RAN" in j["states"]
               and max(j["args"][a]["lam"] / j["args"][a]["mu"] for a in ("baseline", "candidate")) > 0.9]
    exps = [r for r in registry.records if r["kind"] == "experiment" and "verdict" in r["facts"]]
    ab = {k: v["value"] for k, v in exps[0]["facts"].items()} if exps else {}
    hw = ab.get("difference_half_width", float("inf"))
    run_ids = registry.run_ids()
    facts_ok = all(set(f["runs"]) <= run_ids for e in registry.records if e["kind"] == "experiment" for f in e["facts"].values())
    repro = [reg.reproduce(r) for r in registry.runs()]
    found, traced = claims.traced_runs(published, registry)
    recheck = [r for r in claims.review(published, registry)[0] if not r["ok"]]
    overclaim = [r["sentence"] for r in rows if "significan" in r["sentence"] and not r["ok"]]

    score("milestone", "M1 model verified (V&V) + reproducible", all(r["covered"] for r in v_rows) and same,
          checks=v_rows, same_seed_same_bits=same, model=f"{model.NAME}@{model.VERSION}")
    score("milestone", "M2 contract gate before any run", bool(by_contract) and not outside and not runs_rejected,
          rejected_by_contract=by_contract, ran_outside_envelope=outside, runs_for_rejected_jobs=runs_rejected)
    score("milestone", "M3 experiment registry", len(repro) > 0 and facts_ok and all(repro),
          runs=len(repro), experiments=len([r for r in registry.records if r["kind"] == "experiment"]),
          facts_trace_to_runs=facts_ok)
    score("milestone", "M4 replications from target half-width", hw <= HALF_WIDTH and ab.get("replications", 0) >= 10,
          requested=3, replications=ab.get("replications"), diff_half_width=round(hw, 3), target=HALF_WIDTH,
          verdict=ab.get("verdict"), diff=round(ab.get("difference", 0), 3))
    score("milestone", "M5 claim check + published report", bool(rows) and not recheck,
          sentences=len(rows), rejected=[{"sentence": r["sentence"][:60], "reason": r["reason"]} for r in rows if not r["ok"]])
    score("seam", "agent <-> tool schema", bool(by_contract) and not outside, test="tests/test_seam_contract.py")
    score("seam", "agent claims <-> computed statistics", not recheck and all(not r["ok"] for r in rows
          if r["sentence"].startswith("At lam")), test="tests/test_seam_claims.py")
    score("seam", "sim stochasticity <-> conclusions", ab.get("verdict") != "inconclusive" and hw <= HALF_WIDTH
          and not overclaim, verdict=ab.get("verdict"), overclaims_rejected=overclaim, test="tests/test_seam_replications.py")
    score("seam", "cost/time budget", pl.budget.spent <= SIM_BUDGET and out["calls"] <= MAX_CALLS
          and not runs_rejected, rejected_by_budget=by_budget, spent=pl.budget.spent, limit=SIM_BUDGET, agent_calls=out["calls"], ledger=pl.budget.ledger,
          test="tests/test_seam_budget.py")
    score("fitness", "100% of numeric claims traced to a registry run", found > 0 and traced == found,
          numbers=found, traced=traced, test="tests/test_fitness.py::test_claims_traced")
    score("fitness", "every run reproducible bit-for-bit from its seed", repro and all(repro),
          reproduced=sum(repro), runs=len(repro), env=model.ENVIRONMENT, test="tests/test_fitness.py::test_runs_reproducible")
    score("fitness", "budget never exceeded", pl.budget.spent <= SIM_BUDGET
          and sum(a for _, a in pl.budget.ledger) == pl.budget.spent, spent=pl.budget.spent, limit=SIM_BUDGET,
          test="tests/test_fitness.py::test_budget_never_exceeded")
    passed = sum(x["pass"] for x in lines)
    final = {"scorecard": "PASS" if passed == len(lines) else "FAIL", "passed": passed, "total": len(lines),
             "inject": args.inject}
    print(json.dumps(final))
    registry.close()
    (out_dir / "scorecard.jsonl").write_text("".join(json.dumps(x) + "\n" for x in lines + [final]), encoding="utf-8")
    (out_dir / "report.md").write_text(f"# Published summary\n\n{published}\n\n# Agent draft\n\n{out['summary']}\n",
                                   encoding="utf-8")
    return 0 if final["scorecard"] == "PASS" else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

codeWalkthrough.title: contract.validate()
codeWalkthrough.detail: ai-agents L200 #8 schema_check on SCHEMAS (the same dict the model receives as tools), then the cross-field envelope rule lam/mu <= 0.9 a schema cannot express. Problems are returned as data.

codeWalkthrough.title: Pipeline.submit() and job states
codeWalkthrough.detail: PROPOSED -> VALIDATED -> PLANNED -> RAN -> ANALYSED -> DONE, or REJECTED at the contract or the budget. A rejected job has no runs and no cost.

codeWalkthrough.title: SimBudget.reserve() before every batch
codeWalkthrough.detail: Costs are computed by code (customers per run x runs). The first batch must fit or the job is rejected; an extension that does not fit stops the job with budget_limited instead of overspending.

codeWalkthrough.title: _experiment(): keyed streams + sequential replications
codeWalkthrough.detail: Replication i of arm k uses SeedSequence(root, spawn_key=(k, i)); the policy (solution/replications.py) asks for 10 pilots, then n(h/target)^2 until the 95% Welch half-width of the difference <= 0.3.

codeWalkthrough.title: Registry: run_id, value_hex, facts
codeWalkthrough.detail: Each run is keyed by sha256(model, version, params, seed); its mean (math.fsum) is stored as float.hex. Each experiment stores facts with the run ids behind them - the only numbers a summary may quote.

codeWalkthrough.title: claims.check_sentence()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Uncited numbers, unknown ids, numbers not in the cited facts at the written precision, 'significant' on an inconclusive verdict, a wrong direction, a false 'not significant', or a direction without a qualifier -> rejected; code_line() writes the replacement.

codeWalkthrough.title: run_project.py scorecard
codeWalkthrough.detail: One JSON line per milestone, seam and fitness function; --inject flips one gate (few-reps, unseeded, no-contract, no-budget-gate) and the exit code turns 1.

failureLab.inject: python run_project.py --inject few-reps: the pipeline trusts the agent's replications: 3 (pipeline.naive_policy; the same fault ships in replications.py). Only appears because an agent's request meets a stochastic simulator.
failureLab.symptom: The agent's draft: 'Faster service (mu 1.05) cut the mean wait from 4.28 to 2.58 min (-40%), a significant improvement with 3 replications [exp-439c0335].' Every number traces to the registry. Scorecard 10/12: M4 (half-width 1.728 > 0.3) and the stochasticity seam fail; exit 1.
failureLab.diagnose: Arm CIs 4.28 +/- 2.07 and 2.58 +/- 1.05 overlap; the 95% Welch CI of the difference is -3.436 to 0.019 (includes 0) and n = 3 < 10. claims.check_sentence: 'claims significance; computed verdict is inconclusive'; the published text carries the code line ending 'n = 3 per arm: inconclusive.'
failureLab.fix: solution/replications.py: pilot of 10, then n = ceil(n (h/0.3)^2) until met, each extension reserved in the budget first: 3 -> 10 -> 47 -> 55; difference -0.895 +/- 0.293 (-22%), significant decrease; the claim passes.
failureLab.test: labs/L600/03-agent-driven-simulation/tests/test_failure_lab.py (fault reproduces + checker rejects; fixed pipeline supports the claim; --inject few-reps exits 1) and tests/test_build_task.py (shipped replications.py fails 3/3, solution passes)

buildTask.task: Implement required_replications(requested, a, b, half_width) in replications.py: at least N0 = 10 pilot replications, then n x (achieved 95% Welch half-width / target)^2, rounded up; never fewer than requested.
buildTask.acceptance: BUILD_TARGET=mine python -m unittest tests.test_build_task -v -> Ran 3 tests ... OK (shipped file: FAILED (failures=3)); BUILD_TARGET=mine python run_project.py -> PASS 12/12.

scalingLimits: Precision costs 1/h^2: +/-0.2 needs 105 replications per arm (420,000 customers) vs 55 for +/-0.3 - signal: budget_limited true and half-width above target; use CRN (10 replications for +/-0.266 here) with a paired analysis, or relax the target.

Many experiments per session: each 95% CI is per comparison, so 20 A/B jobs expect about one false 'significant' - signal: significant results scattered across arbitrary variants; control the family (Bonferroni) or use ranking-and-selection (simulation L400 #18).

Bit-for-bit only within one environment fingerprint: random.expovariate uses the platform libm log and Python guarantees only random()'s sequence across versions - signal: reproduce() false after an OS/Python upgrade with unchanged code; pin the environment or store tolerances per fingerprint (cross-OS runs pendingCi).

troubleshooting.symptom: M3/F2 fail with reproduced 0 after you edited simulation/labs/L200/10-warmup-replications/warmup.py
troubleshooting.action: Intended: model.VERSION is its hash, so old run ids no longer describe the code. Re-run the session to rebuild the registry.

Small models often drop the [exp-...] citation. That is the checker working; the published text falls back to code-written lines. Strengthen the system prompt or pick a larger model, never relax the check.

troubleshooting.symptom: budget seam fails after you raised the target precision
troubleshooting.action: Raise SIM_BUDGET deliberately (an ADR change) or accept budget_limited; the fitness function must stay green.

agentAssist.task: The whole project is an agent: it proposes run_experiment/run_screening calls and writes the summary; code decides runs, replications, cost and what gets published.
agentAssist.prompt: agent.SYSTEM + the brief: 'Help-desk study, seed 13. Screen with sobol 64. Screen with morris 10. Compare mu 1.0 vs 1.05 at lam 0.8 with 3 replications. Compare mu 1.0 vs 1.05 at lam 0.97 with 3 replications.'
agentAssist.check: contract.validate before running; SimBudget.reserve before every batch; claims.review on every sentence (citation, numbers at written precision, wording vs verdict).
agentAssist.expected: Fake model: 2 of 4 jobs refused (budget, schema); 1 of 4 sentences rejected ('32.3 min', uncited); published report 7/7 traced.
agentAssist.realModelNote: --real-model uses LOCAL_MODEL_URL/LOCAL_MODEL (Ollama's OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions supports tools). Only the brief and tool results are sent. Not run here (no model in the sandbox): pendingCi.

inRealSystems: Simulation studies in operations and engineering use the same discipline - fixed precision targets for replications and documented seeds - before results reach a decision maker; an agent only makes asking cheaper.
Agent platforms validate tool arguments against JSON Schema and keep audit logs of tool calls; the registry here is that audit log with the extra promise that every entry can be re-run.
useWhen: Use this shape whenever a model writes conclusions about numbers you computed: experiments, benchmarks, A/B tests, capacity studies. If the agent can choose the sample size or quote uncited numbers, it can fool you.
simulatorVsReal: The 'real system' is a simulated M/M/1 help desk with a known answer (the formula), which is what makes the claim checker's verdicts checkable here. The fake model is a deterministic rule set that behaves like a naive agent (always says 'significant', invents a textbook number for a rejected run); real models vary run to run, the gates do not.
caution: The agent never decides: it cannot run outside the envelope, choose n, overspend, or publish an unverified sentence. Send it only the brief and tool results - never keys, personal data or raw logs. A 'significant' result is still one comparison at 95%: many agent-chosen comparisons need family-wise control before anyone acts.
checkpoint: PASS: run_project.py prints 12/12 and exits 0; --inject few-reps exits 1 with the overclaim rejected; python -m unittest discover -s tests passes 38 tests; three ADRs, three fitness functions, four seam tests.

checkYourself.q: Every number in the 3-replication sentence traced to the registry. Why was it still rejected?
checkYourself.a: The word 'significant' was false: the 95% CI of the difference (-3.436 to 0.019) includes 0 and n = 3 < 10. Numbers and wording are separate claims.

checkYourself.q: Why does extending from 10 to 55 replications not change the first 10 runs?
checkYourself.a: Seeds are keyed by (root, arm, replication) through SeedSequence spawn_key, so replication i is the same run whatever follows - same run_id, same bits.

checkYourself.q: Why is lam 0.9 / mu 0.95 rejected although both values are inside the schema ranges?
checkYourself.a: Utilisation 0.947 is outside the envelope verified in M1 (<= 0.9). A schema checks fields one at a time; the cross-field rule lives in code.

checkYourself.q: The pipeline stopped at 10 replications with budget_limited. Is the result useless?
checkYourself.a: No: it is reported with its real half-width (0.645), and code decides the verdict from it; what you may not do is quote the +/-0.2 precision you asked for.

conceptSummary: An agent proposes help-desk experiments; a job pipeline decides. Contract gate (schema + verified envelope lam/mu <= 0.9) and budget gate (300,000 customers, reserved first) refuse 2 of 4 jobs at zero cost; keyed seeds and an append-only registry make all 160 runs reproducible bit-for-bit; replications grow 3 -> 55 until the difference CI is +/-0.293 (-22%, significant); the claim checker drops an invented 32.3 min and, in the failure lab, a 'significant improvement' from 3 replications whose CI runs from -3.436 to 0.019.

macMini.gains: Real open-weight models (Ollama on Metal) replace the rule-following fake, so the contract, budget and claim gates are measured against mistakes nobody scripted; and every performance core runs seeded overnight studies (80,000 coverage runs, Sobol at n = 8192) that settle the verified envelope and the smallest trustworthy screening size.

tools.name: Ollama
tools.install: brew install ollama && brew services start ollama (or the app: https://ollama.com/download)

tools.name: Qwen2.5 3b/7b/14b (32b with 32 GB+) via ollama pull

experiments.title: Three real models, one brief, the same gates
experiments.why: The fake always proposes the out-of-envelope arm and always over-claims; a real model may refuse, invent a field, loop or over-claim differently. Each mistake must land on a gate, and the count per model shows where.

steps.title: Size the models
steps.detail: mac_profile.py reads RAM with sysctl and lists the 2-3 largest Qwen2.5 sizes whose Q4_K_M weights + f16 KV cache fit the budget.
steps.mac:
python3 integrated/mac-mini/scripts/mac_profile.py
ollama pull qwen2.5:3b && ollama pull qwen2.5:7b
steps.expected: 16/24 GB: qwen2.5:3b, 7b, 14b; 32/64 GB: 7b, 14b, 32b. ollama ps must show 100% GPU while a model answers.

steps.title: Fake baseline, then the real models
steps.detail: compare_models.py runs the project BRIEF through the unchanged pipeline and claim checker once per model and writes one JSON line each.
steps.mac:
cd integrated/labs/L600/03-agent-driven-simulation/mac_mini
python3 compare_models.py --here
LOCAL_MODEL_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1 python3 compare_models.py --auto
steps.expected: Fake row: contract_rejected 1, budget_rejected 1, claims_dropped 1, budget_spent 270000. Real rows differ per model; published_traced must equal numbers_found and budget_respected must be true for every model (exit 1 otherwise: a gate failure, not a model failure).

steps.title: Full scorecard with one real model
steps.detail: The existing --real-model switch; M2 needs a contract rejection, which a careful model may not produce.
steps.expected: Fitness lines (claims traced, runs reproducible, budget) pass; M2 may FAIL if the model avoided the out-of-envelope arm - the known gap, now measured.

experiments.measure: Per model: contract_rejected, budget_rejected, claims_dropped / claims_total, budget_spent of 300,000, agent_calls of 8, stopped.
experiments.decides: ADR-0001 gets a measured-with-real-models note; if models avoid the bad arm, M2 gets a scripted bad proposal instead of relying on the model; MAX_CALLS changes only if a model needs all 8 calls for a valid plan.

experiments.title: Does the 95 % CI cover 95 % of the time across the envelope?
experiments.why: M1 checks one 10-replication CI per utilisation. Coverage is a property of the procedure (warm-up, run length, replications) and only thousands of independent repetitions show it; the start-up transient biases short runs at high rho.

steps.title: Determinism check
steps.detail: Seeds come from (root, experiment, replication), never from the worker, so the hash of all values is identical for any pool size.
steps.expected: values_sha256_16 identical with --workers 1 and with all cores.

steps.title: Overnight coverage study
steps.detail: 4 utilisations x 2000 experiments x 10 replications of 20,000 customers (M1's design) on every performance core.
steps.expected: Per rho: coverage, bias and z_vs_95 = (coverage - 0.95) / sqrt(0.95*0.05/2000). |z| < 2 is consistent with 95 %; falling coverage with positive bias as rho rises is the initial transient.

experiments.measure: Coverage and bias at rho 0.5, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9 (2000 experiments each).
experiments.decides: contract.RHO_MAX (verified envelope, now 0.9): if coverage at 0.9 is clearly below 0.95 (z < -3), lower RHO_MAX or lengthen M1's warm-up/run; recorded in ADR-0003.

experiments.title: Smallest trustworthy Sobol screening size
experiments.why: The brief asks for sobol 64 and the schema allows size >= 2; with 1,000-customer runs small-n rankings can be noise. A large-n reference settles which size to allow.

steps.title: Reference run
steps.detail: Same screening function and CRN seed as pipeline._screening, base sizes n/8, n/4, n/2, n.
steps.expected: Rows for n = 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192 with ST per input, ranking and matches_reference; the first n from which every row is true is the smallest stable size for these ranges.

experiments.measure: Smallest n whose ranking matches the n = 8192 reference; ST(lam) and ST(mu) at 8192.
experiments.decides: The run_screening schema minimum for sobol and SIM_BUDGET together (n x 6 x 1,000 customers <= 300,000 allows n <= 50 today), or a pipeline rule that reports 'ranking not stable at this n' instead of a ranking.

macMini.overnight: caffeinate -i python3 overnight_sweep.py both --experiments 2000 --n 8192: 80,000 coverage runs of 20,000 customers plus Sobol at four sizes on every performance core. It reveals the procedure's real CI coverage across the envelope and the smallest trustworthy screening size, and its hashes test bit-for-bit reproducibility against another machine (ADR-0002).
